title: Nine heads where Roman and Reformed schools commonly agree
source_text: LII. Ex iis vero quae jam exposita sunt, manifestum est Doctores, tam Scholae Romanae, quam Scholae Reformatae, agnoscere communi consensu, 1. Fidem recte distingui in mortuam & vivam, otiosam & activam; unam quae est bonis operibus vacua, alteram vero quae per dilectionem operatur, & secum involvit fiduciam in Deum. 2. Solam fidem vivam justificare, mortuam autem nihil ad justitiam & salutem prodesse. 3. Non solum credendi actum praecise sumptum, sed multos alios quoque, qui ad veram poenitentiam, & seriam ad Deum conversionem concurrunt, esse conditiones a Deo praerequisitas, ut aliquis ab eo peccatorum veniam & infusionem novae & habitualis justitiae impetret. 4. Remissionem peccatorum, & renovationem interioris hominis esse donum Dei mere gratuitum; quod nec fidei, nec ullis operibus quantumcunque ex gratia Dei factis, ex justitia debetur. 5. Divinae bonitati & sapientiae congruum & conveniens esse, ut peccatori quem serio poenitet, & qui per fidem ad Dei misericordiam confugit, remittantur peccata, & Spiritus Sancti gratia donetur: non vero incredulis & impoenitentibus. 6. Novam justitiam quam Spiritus Sanctus in fidelibus creat, constare non solo fidei habitu, sed etiam reliquis virtutibus Christianis. 7. Justitiam illam exercitio bonorum operum non conservari solum, sed etiam augeri, illosque qui gratia jam accepta recte utentes, bonis operibus vacant, ampliorem in dies gratiam accipere. 8. Justitiam quae per Spiritus Sancti gratiam fidelibus inest, veram & synceram esse, non tantum hominum, sed Dei ipsius judicio: adeoque fore ut Deus, quum judicabit vivos & mortuos, solenne & gloriosum testimonium illi perhibeat, & vitae aeternae praemium retribuat. 9. Nullam esse in piis justitiam quae possit ferre rigidum judicii divini examen, si Deus hominem absque misericordia judicet, & erga ipsum nulla indulgentia & clementia uti velit.
pass_a_gloss: But from those things which have now been set forth, it is manifest that the Doctors, both of the Roman School and of the Reformed School, acknowledge by common consent: (1) that faith is rightly distinguished into dead and living, idle and active—one empty of good works, the other working through love and involving trust in God with itself; (2) that only living faith justifies, while dead faith profits nothing toward righteousness and salvation; (3) that not only the act of believing precisely taken, but also many other acts which concur toward true repentance and serious conversion to God, are conditions prerequisite by God that someone obtain from him pardon of sins and infusion of new and habitual righteousness; (4) that remission of sins and renovation of the interior man is a merely gratuitous gift of God, owed from justice neither to faith nor to any works howsoever done from God's grace; (5) that it is fitting and suitable to divine goodness and wisdom that sins be remitted and the grace of the Holy Spirit given to the sinner who seriously repents and flees by faith to God's mercy—not to the unbelieving and impenitent; (6) that the new righteousness which the Holy Spirit creates in the faithful consists not in the habit of faith alone but also in the remaining Christian virtues; (7) that that righteousness is not only conserved but also increased by the exercise of good works, and that those who rightly using grace already received devote themselves to good works receive ampler grace day by day; (8) that the righteousness which is in the faithful through the Holy Spirit's grace is true and sincere, not only in men's judgment but in God's own: and so it will be that God, when he judges the living and the dead, will bear solemn and glorious witness to it and repay the reward of eternal life; (9) that there is in the godly no righteousness that can bear the rigid examination of divine judgment if God should judge a man without mercy and will to use toward him no indulgence and clemency.
pass_b_english: Nine shared heads: living vs dead faith; only living justifies; repentant conditions; free gift of remission/renovation; fitting mercy to penitents; virtues beyond faith-habit; growth by good works; true Spirit-wrought righteousness God will vindicate; yet none stands strict judgment without mercy.
